stem: A team's Athena queries over a large CSV dataset in S3 are scanning far more data, and costing far more, than the team expects for the columns each query actually needs.

choices.text: Increase the number of shards behind the ingestion stream
Move the dataset into AWS Glue DataBrew for permanent storage
Convert the dataset to Parquet with a Glue ETL job or an Athena CTAS query
Enable enhanced fan-out for the Athena queries

rationale: Converting the dataset from row-based CSV into columnar Parquet, via a Glue ETL job or an Athena CTAS query, lets Athena read only the columns and byte ranges a query needs, which cuts the data scanned and the resulting cost. Increasing shard count is a Kinesis Data Streams ingestion concept and has no effect on how an already-landed S3 dataset is scanned by Athena. DataBrew is a data-preparation tool, not a permanent storage location, and moving data into it does not change its file format. Enhanced fan-out is a Kinesis Data Streams consumer feature; Athena queries have no such setting at all.
